area: Hollow Horizon terrain, trees and scatter (tools/gen_worldgen.py)

findings.symptom: "the trees look too blocky and unnatural... allow them to have more than one block thick trunk"
findings.root_cause: Every one of the four groves is built by the single helper `_tree()`, which only ever emits `minecraft:straight_trunk_placer` or `minecraft:forking_trunk_placer`. Both place exactly ONE log per horizontal layer — StraightTrunkPlacer.placeTrunk loops `placeLog(origin.above(y))`, ForkingTrunkPlacer adds a lean and one side branch but is still a single column. No thick-trunk placer is used anywhere in the mod, and there is no custom Java trunk placer (the only file under src/main/java/com/echoingvoid/worldgen is HollowHorizonTeleporter.java).

The complete registered set in 26.2 is TrunkPlacerType.java:8-18: straight, forking, giant, mega_jungle, dark_oak, fancy, bending, upwards_branching, cherry. Reading each placeTrunk, exactly THREE put more than one log in a horizontal layer, and all three are 2x2:

findings.fix:
Two-part change, both in tools/gen_worldgen.py.
(a) Widen `_tree()` at gen_worldgen.py:1439-1443 so `placer` can be one of the 2x2 types, and re-target the species. Vanilla parameter sets, copied exactly from C:/Projects/mcref-26.2/assets/data/minecraft/worldgen/configured_feature/:
  mega_spruce.json      : giant_trunk_placer      base_height 13, height_rand_a 2,  height_rand_b 14
  mega_jungle_tree.json : mega_jungle_trunk_placer base_height 10, height_rand_a 2,  height_rand_b 19
  dark_oak.json         : dark_oak_trunk_placer   base_height 6,  height_rand_a 2,  height_rand_b 1
  cherry.json           : cherry_trunk_placer     base_height 7, height_rand_a 1, height_rand_b 0, branch_count weighted_list {1:1, 2:1, 3:1}, branch_horizontal_length uniform 2..4, branch_start_offset_from_top {min -4, max -3}, branch_end_offset_from_top uniform -1..0
  mangrove.json         : upwards_branching_trunk_placer base_height 2, height_rand_a 1, height_rand_b 4, place_branch_per_log_probability 0.5, extra_branch_steps uniform 1..4, extra_branch_length uniform 0..1
(b) To get the variable 1 / 2 / 4+ thickness the player asked for, do NOT try to do it in one configured_feature — no vanilla trunk_placer varies its own width. Emit 2-3 variants per species and select between them, either with a `minecraft:random_selector` / `minecraft:simple_random_selector` configured feature, or by listing several `*_grove_placed` features in the biome with different rarity_filters. A ~60/30/10 split of straight (1x1) / dark_oak (2x2, leaning) / mega_jungle (2x2 + branches) reproduces the silhouette variety the player is describing.
For the "above four thick near the ground" flare, the only data-driven vanilla mechanism is the tree config's optional `root_placer` field, `minecraft:mangrove_root_placer` (the sole entry in RootPlacerType.java). mangrove.json uses max_root_width 8, max_root_length 15, random_skew_chance 0.2, trunk_offset_y uniform 1..3 — that produces a splayed base up to 8 wide under a 1-thick trunk. It requires a root block state and a `can_grow_through` HolderSet; note MangroveRootPlacer.placeRoots returning false aborts the whole tree (TreeFeature.java:76-78), so the can_grow_through set must include the mod's surface blocks or trees will silently stop generating.

findings.symptom: "like the way the trees in the nether are generated, they have more organic trunks that sometimes are one or two thick, but can go above four thick near the ground"
findings.root_cause: The nether trees the player is referencing are NOT tree features and have no trunk_placer at all, so there is no placer to copy. minecraft:crimson_fungus and minecraft:warped_fungus are `minecraft:huge_fungus` features whose stem width is hard-coded in Java: HugeFungusFeature.placeStem uses `int stemRadius = isHuge ? 1 : 0`, i.e. 1x1 normally and 3x3 for the rare huge variant, with the 4 corner columns of the 3x3 filled only at 10% per block — that ragged corner is precisely the "organic, sometimes one or two thick" look. `isHuge = !config.planted && random.nextFloat() < 0.06F`, so only 6% of naturally generated fungi are the wide kind. Height is `Mth.nextInt(random, 4, 13)`, doubled on a 1-in-12 roll.
findings.evidence:
C:/Projects/mcref-26.2/assets/data/minecraft/worldgen/configured_feature/crimson_fungus.json and warped_fungus.json — both are `"type": "minecraft:huge_fungus"` with config keys decor_state, hat_state, replaceable_blocks, stem_state, valid_base_block ONLY. There is no trunk_placer, foliage_placer, or minimum_size field. (Note there is no huge_crimson_fungus.json / warped_fungi.json in 26.2 — the file names are crimson_fungus.json / warped_fungus.json.)

findings.fix:
Do not expect a JSON tree config to reproduce this. Pick one of two routes:
(1) Data-only, closest achievable: as in the previous finding, emit per-species variants and randomise between them — straight_trunk_placer (1 thick), dark_oak_trunk_placer or mega_jungle_trunk_placer (2 thick), plus a mangrove_root_placer flare for the wide base. Weight them so the thick ones are the minority, mirroring vanilla's 6%.
(2) Faithful: register a mod Feature in Java that mirrors HugeFungusFeature.placeStem — a per-tree `stemRadius` sampled from a weighted list (0 / 1 / 2) and a probabilistic corner fill, which is what actually gives 1 / 3 / 5-wide organic trunks. The mod has no custom Feature today, so this is new Java plus a FeatureType registration; gen_worldgen.py would then emit the config JSON for it.

findings.symptom: "make the leaves spawn in more varied formations, some holes some imperfections less blocky"
findings.root_cause: All four groves use `minecraft:blob_foliage_placer` with CONSTANT radius, CONSTANT offset 0 and CONSTANT height. BlobFoliagePlacer draws axis-aligned square rows (`placeLeavesRow` iterates dx,dz over the full square) and its only irregularity is `shouldSkipLocation`, which trims a block ONLY at the four extreme corners, and even then only half the time: `return dx == currentRadius && dz == currentRadius && (random.nextInt(2) == 0 || y == 0);`. With radius 2 or 3 that means at most one corner voxel per quadrant per layer is ever missing — the result is a near-perfect cuboid. Nothing in the config can introduce interior holes, because BlobFoliagePlacer has no hole parameters.
findings.evidence:
tools/gen_worldgen.py:1445-1451 — `foliage_placer: dict = {"type": f"minecraft:{foliage}", "radius": radius, "offset": 0}` / `foliage_placer["height"] = height`. Actual generated values (src/main/resources/data/echoing_void/worldgen/configured_feature/): amber_bough radius 3 height 3; echo_ash radius 2 height 3; humming radius 2 height 4; petrified radius 2 height 3 — all offset 0, all blob_foliage_placer.
C:/Projects/mcref-26.2/sources/.../foliageplacers/BlobFoliagePlacer.java:64 shouldSkipLocation (quoted above) and FoliagePlacer.java:108-115 placeLeavesRow (full square scan).
FoliagePlacer.java:27-30 shows radius and offset are `IntProviders.codec(0, 16)` — i.e. they ACCEPT a uniform/weighted provider, so the constants are a choice, not a limit.
findings.fix:
In tools/gen_worldgen.py:1445-1451, switch the foliage type per species and pass IntProviders instead of bare ints. Vanilla placers that produce exactly the holes and imperfections asked for, with their shipped parameters:
  * minecraft:cherry_foliage_placer (cherry.json) — radius 4, offset 0, height 5, wide_bottom_layer_hole_chance 0.25, corner_hole_chance 0.25, hanging_leaves_chance 0.16666667, hanging_leaves_extension_chance 0.33333334. This is the only placer with explicit hole probabilities; CherryFoliagePlacer.shouldSkipLocation punches the wide bottom layer and the corners, and placeLeavesRowWithHangingLeavesBelow adds ragged hanging strands.
  * minecraft:random_spread_foliage_placer (mangrove.json / azalea_tree.json) — radius 3, offset 0, foliage_height 2, leaf_placement_attempts 70 (50 for azalea). RandomSpreadFoliagePlacer.createFoliage just throws N leaves at random offsets and never fills a row, so the canopy is inherently gappy — this is the strongest "less blocky" option.
  * minecraft:fancy_foliage_placer (fancy_oak.json) — radius 2, offset 4, height 4. FancyFoliagePlacer.shouldSkipLocation is `square(dx+0.5) + square(dz+0.5) > currentRadius^2`, i.e. a true circular cross-section rather than a square one.
Also make radius vary per tree, e.g. `"radius": {"type": "minecraft:uniform", "min_inclusive": 2, "max_inclusive": 4}` — legal because the codec is an IntProvider, and it stops every tree in a grove being the same size.
Combining a branching trunk placer (cherry / mega_jungle / dark_oak / upwards_branching) with any of these matters more than the foliage placer alone: those placers return MULTIPLE FoliageAttachments, so the canopy becomes several overlapping blobs instead of one, which is most of the "varied formation" effect.

findings.symptom: Pre-emptive: a naive switch to a 2x2 trunk placer will make trees stop generating entirely rather than get thicker
findings.root_cause: `_tree()` hard-codes `two_layers_feature_size` with `limit: 1, lower_size: 0, upper_size: 2`. TreeFeature.getMaxFreeTreeHeight asks minimumSize.getSizeAtHeight(h, y) for a radius r and requires every block in [-r..r]^2 to be free; with lower_size 0 the check at y=0 only tests the single origin column. That is fine for a 1x1 trunk, but a 2x2 placer writes into (+1,0), (0,+1), (+1,+1) which were never tested, so the tree either overwrites neighbouring terrain or, once the free-height check clips (`return y - 2`), doPlace bails because clippedTreeHeight < treeHeight and minClippedHeight is absent.
findings.evidence:
tools/gen_worldgen.py:1480-1482 — `"minimum_size": {"type": "minecraft:two_layers_feature_size", "limit": 1, "lower_size": 0, "upper_size": 2}` for all four species.
C:/Projects/mcref-26.2/sources/.../TreeFeature.java:95-112 getMaxFreeTreeHeight, and :73-75 `if (clippedTreeHeight >= treeHeight || !minClippedHeight.isEmpty() && clippedTreeHeight >= minClippedHeight.getAsInt())`.
TwoLayersFeatureSize.java:41-43 `getSizeAtHeight` returns lowerSize below `limit`, upperSize above.
What vanilla actually ships for its 2x2 trees: mega_spruce.json and mega_jungle_tree.json use `two_layers_feature_size {lower_size: 1, upper_size: 2}` (limit defaults to 1); dark_oak.json and pale_oak.json use `three_layers_feature_size {upper_size: 2}` (limit 1, upper_limit 1, lower_size 0, middle_size 1 by default).
findings.fix: When changing the placer in tools/gen_worldgen.py:1480-1482, change the size with it: use `{"type": "minecraft:two_layers_feature_size", "lower_size": 1, "upper_size": 2}` for giant_trunk_placer / mega_jungle_trunk_placer, and `{"type": "minecraft:three_layers_feature_size", "upper_size": 2}` for dark_oak_trunk_placer. Separately, the `spacing` ring built in tree_placement (gen_worldgen.py:1499-1503) only tests the four cardinal offsets at r=2..spacing; a 2x2 trunk occupies +1,+1 diagonally, so spacing should go up by 1 for the thick variants.

findings.symptom: "i dont really like the random artifacts that generate atop the floating island biome... they spawn far too frequently, they need to spawn at a twentieth the density"
findings.root_cause: `cavern_debris_placed` is the biggest source and it is NOT confined to caves despite its name. It uses `minecraft:count_on_every_layer` with count 2. CountOnEveryLayerPlacement starts its downward scan at the MOTION_BLOCKING height and calls findOnGroundYPosition with layerToPlaceOn = 0 first — LAYER 0 IS THE TOP SURFACE OF THE ISLAND. It then loops, incrementing the layer, until a pass finds nothing, so it also drops 2 heaps on every interior ledge in the column. The feature it places is `fallen_debris`, a `minecraft:block_pile` of raw_phonolite / echo_slate / amber_strata / resonant_chalk / chime_sand — bare rock heaps sitting on the grass, which is exactly what "random artifacts" describes. BlockPileFeature spans `2 + rand(2)` in each horizontal direction and 2 blocks high, so each heap is up to 7x7x2.
findings.evidence:
tools/gen_worldgen.py:1829-1836 — `write(pf / "cavern_debris_placed.json", {... {"type": "minecraft:count_on_every_layer", "count": 2}, m_filter(p_all(p_replaceable(), p_tag(NATURAL_GROUND, (0, -1, 0)))), ...})` — line 1832 is the count.
It is in the UNDERGROUND_DECORATION list of Resonant Plains (gen_worldgen.py:1318) and Shattered Octaves (gen_worldgen.py:1354). Shattered Octaves is the floating-island biome (BIOME_OCTAVES, gen_worldgen.py:184, described at :1329-1331 as "many smaller islands").
C:/Projects/mcref-26.2/sources/.../placement/CountOnEveryLayerPlacement.java:41-58 — `int layer = 0; do { ... int y = findOnGroundYPosition(context, x, startY, z, layer); ... layer++; } while (foundAny);` and :67-84 findOnGroundYPosition returning the FIRST empty-over-solid boundary from the top when layerToPlaceOn == 0.
C:/Projects/mcref-26.2/sources/.../BlockPileFeature.java:28-38 — `int xr = 2 + random.nextInt(2); int zr = 2 + random.nextInt(2);` over `origin.offset(-xr,0,-zr)` to `origin.offset(xr,1,zr)`.
The rubble state list is tools/gen_worldgen.py:1793-1805.
findings.fix:
tools/gen_worldgen.py:1832. `count_on_every_layer` takes an IntProvider (CountOnEveryLayerPlacement.java:17, `IntProviders.codec(0, 256)`), so one twentieth is expressed as a weighted list rather than a fraction: replace `{"type": "minecraft:count_on_every_layer", "count": 2}` with `{"type": "minecraft:count_on_every_layer", "count": {"type": "minecraft:weighted_list", "distribution": [{"data": 0, "weight": 9}, {"data": 1, "weight": 1}]}}` — mean 0.1 vs the current 2.0, exactly 1/20.
Caveat: because the `do { } while (foundAny)` loop terminates as soon as one pass places nothing, a low count also truncates how deep the layer walk goes, so deep cave floors lose debris too. If the debris is wanted underground but not on top, the cleaner fix is to keep count 2 and add a guard to the filter at gen_worldgen.py:1833 that requires something solid overhead — i.e. reuse the `beneath_something` predicate defined at gen_worldgen.py:1814-1815.

findings.symptom: Same symptom — the second scatter feature that is explicitly aimed at island tops
findings.root_cause: `island_debris_placed` is the TOP_LAYER_MODIFICATION feature in all three biomes and asks for `count: 8` block_pile heaps per chunk. Its block_predicate_filter also demands `beneath_something` — solid at +7, +11 or +15 — and because the position comes from the OCEAN_FLOOR_WG heightmap (the topmost motion-blocking block in the column) there is by construction nothing solid above it, so this guard should reject almost every attempt. That makes count 8 the loud number if the guard is ever relaxed, and it means this feature is probably NOT what the player is seeing today.

findings.symptom: Same symptom — third candidate, ranked lowest but by far the highest raw count
findings.root_cause: `bismuth_cluster_dense_placed` runs 40 attempts per chunk in Shattered Octaves (22 in the other two biomes) over `height_range uniform 6..200`, and each attempt does an `environment_scan` of up to 12 steps through air to the first solid block, then offsets 1 block off it. Any of those 40 start positions that lands within 12 blocks of an island's upper surface will plant a bismuth_cluster on top of it. If the "artifacts" the player means are glowing crystal shards rather than rock heaps, this is the source.
findings.evidence:
tools/gen_worldgen.py:1736 — `for suffix, count in (("", 22), ("_dense", 40)):` writing bismuth_cluster_placed / bismuth_cluster_dense_placed with `{"type": "minecraft:count", "count": count}` and `{"type": "minecraft:height_range", "height": _uniform(6, 200)}` (gen_worldgen.py:1740-1744).

findings.fix: If confirmed as the culprit, tools/gen_worldgen.py:1736 — change the tuple to `(("", 22), ("_dense", 2))` for 1/20 of the dense count, or better, leave the count alone and stop the scan reaching the surface: lower the height_range ceiling at gen_worldgen.py:1742 from `_uniform(6, 200)` to something below the island tops (roughly y 6..120 given the surface sits near y100-140), so a start position can never be within 12 blocks of open sky. I did not verify which of the three features the player is actually looking at — I would confirm by generating a chunk and checking whether the surface litter is rock heaps (debris) or crystals (bismuth).

findings.symptom: "wants vanilla-like CAVE generation in the dimension"
findings.root_cause: The dimension has NO carvers at all. write_biome hard-codes `"carvers": []` for every biome and there is no configured_carver directory anywhere in the mod. What the dimension DOES have is the noise-router half of caves — the `caves`/`underground` density functions faithfully reproduce NoiseRouterData's overworld cave stack (cheese, entrances, spaghetti_2d, spaghetti roughness, pillars, noodle) — so the dimension already produces vanilla's noise caverns, but not the winding carver tunnels and ravines that players actually recognise as "caves". The noise settings themselves are correct in shape; the missing piece is entirely on the biome side.
findings.evidence:
tools/gen_worldgen.py:1245 — `"carvers": [],` in write_biome, applied to all three biomes. Confirmed in the generated output: src/main/resources/data/echoing_void/worldgen/biome/resonant_plains.json:2 is `"carvers": [],`. `grep -rn carver tools/*.py` returns exactly one hit, that line. `find src/main/resources -path "*carver*"` returns nothing.
The noise-cave terms that DO exist: tools/gen_worldgen.py:958-977 build `underground.json` and `caves.json` using minecraft:overworld/caves/entrances, spaghetti_2d, spaghetti_roughness_function, pillars (constants at :487-492), and gen_worldgen.py:1146-1150 wires them in as `terrain = max(min(caves, chasms), sky_islands)` with `final_density = min(post_process(slide(terrain)), minecraft:overworld/caves/noodle)`. Cave generosity constants at :309-311 (CAVE_CHEESE_BIAS 0.18, CAVE_LAYER_WEIGHT 3.4, vs vanilla 0.27 / 4.0 per the comment).
Vanilla for comparison: C:/Projects/mcref-26.2/assets/data/minecraft/worldgen/biome/plains.json has `"carvers": ["minecraft:cave", "minecraft:cave_extra_underground", "minecraft:canyon"]` (lush_caves.json is identical; nether_wastes.json uses the single-string form `"minecraft:nether_cave"`; the_end.json is `[]`). The overworld noise_settings JSON has NO carver field at all — its top-level keys are exactly aquifers_enabled, default_block, default_fluid, disable_mob_generation, legacy_random_source, noise, noise_router, ore_veins_enabled, sea_level, spawn_target, surface_rule. Carvers live only on biomes; BiomeGenerationSettings.java:31 decodes `"carvers"` as a HolderSet<ConfiguredWorldCarver>.
Vanilla's carver configs (C:/Projects/mcref-26.2/assets/data/minecraft/worldgen/configured_carver/): cave.json type minecraft:cave, probability 0.15, y uniform {above_bottom 8}..{absolute 180}, yScale uniform 0.1..0.9, horizontal_radius_multiplier uniform 0.7..1.4, vertical_radius_multiplier uniform 0.8..1.3, floor_level uniform -1.0..-0.4, lava_level {above_bottom 8}, replaceable #minecraft:overworld_carver_replaceables. cave_extra_underground.json is identical except probability 0.07 and y max {absolute 47}. canyon.json type minecraft:canyon, probability 0.01, y uniform absolute 10..67, yScale 3.0, vertical_rotation uniform -0.125..0.125, shape {distance_factor uniform 0.75..1.0, horizontal_radius_factor uniform 0.75..1.0, thickness trapezoid min 0 max 6 plateau 2, vertical_radius_center_factor 0.0, vertical_radius_default_factor 1.0, width_smoothness 3}.
Carvers run at ChunkStatus.CARVERS, after SURFACE and before FEATURES (ChunkStatus.java:26-28), and NoiseBasedChunkGenerator.applyCarvers:338-346 iterates `sourceBiomeGenerationSettings.getCarvers()` — an empty list means the whole pass is a no-op.
findings.fix:
Three additions to tools/gen_worldgen.py:
1. Emit configured carvers under MOD/"worldgen"/"configured_carver"/. Copy vanilla cave.json and canyon.json verbatim EXCEPT two fields (see next finding): `replaceable` and `lava_level`. Retune `y` to this dimension's actual rock band — the continent surface sits near y100-140 and the deep strata run to about y48 (the Knell comment at gen_worldgen.py:1679-1682 records that 90% of phonolite is at y48-95), so cave y uniform {absolute 40}..{absolute 130} and canyon y uniform {absolute 55}..{absolute 115} are the analogues of vanilla's 8..180 and 10..67. Vanilla's absolute 180 / 47 / 67 are meaningless here because this dimension's min_y is 0 and height is 256 (gen_worldgen.py:244-245).
2. Change write_biome (tools/gen_worldgen.py:1225-1245) to take a `carvers` argument and write it at line 1245 instead of the hard-coded `[]`, then pass `[ev("hollow_cave"), ev("hollow_canyon")]` from the three gen_biomes calls.
3. Optionally loosen the noise caverns back toward vanilla by raising CAVE_CHEESE_BIAS from 0.18 to 0.27 and CAVE_LAYER_WEIGHT from 3.4 to 4.0 (gen_worldgen.py:310-311) — but be aware of the reason they were lowered, recorded in the comment at :306-309: a thin conical island that is also hollow is a shell the player falls through. Carvers are the safer lever than the cheese bias here.

findings.symptom: Pre-emptive: a straight copy of vanilla's carvers into this dimension will carve nothing, and will flood the world floor with lava
findings.root_cause: Two concrete incompatibilities. (a) WorldCarver.carveBlock refuses any block not in `configuration.replaceable`; vanilla's carvers use #minecraft:overworld_carver_replaceables, whose members are #minecraft:base_stone_overworld, #minecraft:substrate_overworld, sand, terracotta, the iron/copper ore tags, snow, water, gravel, sandstone, calcite, packed_ice and friends. None of the Hollow Horizon's rock (echoing_void:raw_phonolite, echo_slate, amber_strata, resonant_chalk) is in it, and the mod does not extend that tag — src/main/resources/data/minecraft/tags/block/ contains only fence_gates, incorrect_for_diamond_tool, leaves, logs, mineable/, needs_*_tool, planks, slabs, stairs, walls, wooden_*. findings.symptom: "the outpost buildings some of them generate levitating high above their islands" — the residual 3-7 block gap that survives even when the island IS underneath
findings.root_cause:
bridge_stair's two jigsaws are 4 blocks apart in local Y (entry at local y=3, exit at local y=7), so connecting through it yields deltaY = +4. In JigsawPlacement.Placer, for a rigid->rigid link the child's beard reference is computed as

    targetGroundLevelDelta = sourceGroundLevelDelta - deltaY;

and Beardifier then uses `int groundY = box.minY() + groundLevelDelta;`. forge_hall starts with the default groundLevelDelta of 1 (StructurePoolElement.getGroundLevelDelta returns 1; SinglePoolElement does not override it). A bridge_span link has deltaY = 0 so the delta survives as 1, but every bridge_stair link subtracts 4. So a building one stair-bridge out gets groundLevelDelta = 1 - 4 = -3, and its beard target is 3 blocks BELOW the bottom of its own bounding box — i.e. beard_thin deliberately stops 4 blocks short of the building's floor. Two stair bridges in a chain gives -7.

Because every element is rigid the delta is never reset; in vanilla a terrain_matching element resets it (the else branch is `targetGroundLevelDelta = targetElement.getGroundLevelDelta()`), which is why village chains never accumulate.

Separately, beard_thin can never bridge a large drop at all: Beardifier.BEARD_KERNEL_RADIUS = 12 and getBeardContribution returns 0 unless dy+12 is in [0,24). So the beard reaches at most ~12 blocks below the piece's ground reference, and its peak contribution is only ~+0.56 density (value ~0.707 * kernel ~0.98 * the 0.8 scale factor) — nowhere near enough to fill the deep negative density of the void between islands.

findings.root_cause:
The sky-island band and the mainland surface band are allowed to occupy the same altitudes, and where they do not overlap they are separated by an unclimbable gap. The two bands are set by independent constants and were never reconciled.

Mainland top: the surface is where depth crosses zero, depth_top = y_clamped_gradient(1.5@y0, -1.5@y256) + surface_offset, so y_surface = 85.33 * (1.5 + surface_offset). surface_offset = clamp(-0.09 + 0.58*erosion + 0.22*island_mass + height_jitter + 0.06*rim, -1.30, 0.80) - 0.13*sky_present.
  Resonant Plains (erosion -1.0..0.22, the outpost's only biome): offset ~ -0.73..+0.32 -> ground y ~66..155.
  Chalk Reaches (erosion 0.22..1.0): offset up to -0.09+0.58+0.22+0.06 = 0.77 -> ground y ~194.

Sky islands: mask (ceiling +1.30) added to min(top limb, bottom limb). The bottom limb runs -2.20 at y150 to +1.10 at y210, so an island can exist only where the limb clears -1.30, i.e. from y ~166 upward; tops sit at 208-220. SKY_ROUGHNESS 0.62 * base_3d_noise then jitters the underside by roughly +/-15 blocks either way.

Consequence 1 (clipping): Chalk Reaches ground at ~194 sits squarely inside the 166-220 island band, so islands merge into the plateau there. At the top of Resonant Plains' range (155) plus downward roughness on the island underside (~151) the two bands also touch.
Consequence 2 (unreachable): in the body of Resonant Plains the ground is y66-155 and the island tops are y208-220 — a 55 to 150 block vertical gap with nothing in between, so an outpost that lands on a sky island cannot be reached without building up to it.

Move SKY_BOTTOM_FROM at line 327 from (-2.20, 150) to about (-2.20, 175) so the earliest an island can exist is ~y196+, or lower the surface_offset clamp ceiling at line 909 from 0.80 to ~0.55 (mainland ceiling ~175) and leave the sky band alone. findings.root_cause: The trigger is an ABSOLUTE tick window: `Math.abs(interval - 10) <= 3`, i.e. the gap between two consecutive breaks must land in [7,13] ticks. But the achievable gap in vanilla is fully determined by block hardness and tool mining speed: interval = 6 + ceil(30*hardness/speed) ticks (5 ticks of post-break `destroyDelay`, 1 tick to re-acquire the target, then ceil(1/progressPerTick) progress ticks). The window is therefore satisfiable only when hardness <= 7*speed/30 — 2.1 for the Harmonic (speed 9.0), 2.33 for the Knell (speed 10.0). Everything harder is permanently out of band, and instantly-mineable blocks collapse to a 1-tick cadence which is also out of band. The Hollow Horizon strata, where the Knell pickaxe is actually used, is almost entirely above that ceiling.

findings.symptom: Even on stone, where the window is theoretically satisfiable, the ability still refuses to fire during real mining.
findings.root_cause: Every block break with the pickaxe in main hand feeds the beat, unfiltered — including instant-break clutter. `Item.mineBlock` is called unconditionally for every survival break (ServerPlayerGameMode.java:299 has no hardness or tool-correctness precondition), so brushing a torch, a plant, resonance_moss or leaves mid-tunnel records a ~1-tick or wildly-off interval, and line 90 zeroes the streak. Because STREAK_TO_SHATTER requires TWO consecutive on-tempo intervals (three consecutive breaks) with no interruption, a single stray break anywhere in the phrase kills it. The Hollow Horizon surface is specifically carpeted with instant-break cross growths and 0.4-hardness moss/lichen (ModTerrainBlocks.java:158,166,194,203).

(2) The shatter itself destroys the eight neighbours, so the player is now looking into a 3x3 hole; the next target is a block deeper and the crosshair has to re-acquire it, which perturbs the interval and resets the streak. There is also no charge-up/armed cue: the only feedback is the AMETHYST_BLOCK_CHIME played after the fact (:172), so a player who is off-tempo gets no signal that a rhythm is being tracked at all.
